name: MatX
h1_tail: Funding Rounds, Share Prices and Ownership
description: MatX is privately held and has no ticker. Review the price of each funding round, its investors, and the points to confirm before buying or selling.
ledes: MatX is a privately held semiconductor company. Its shares are not listed on an exchange and have no quoted market price; the principal public reference points are the prices at which the company has raised capital. Its most recent financing, a $500 million Series B round announced on February 24, 2026, was made at a valuation the company did not disclose.

Based in Mountain View, California, MatX develops chips for training and running large language models. Existing shares change hands in privately negotiated transactions and remain subject to the company's transfer restrictions.
table_note: MatX has not disclosed the valuation of any round. The seed and Series A rounds were first reported by TechCrunch, and the Series A valuation and amount are as reported by TechCrunch in November 2024.
round_notes: In August 2026, Reuters reported that MatX was seeking to raise new capital at a valuation of $4 billion. MatX has not announced a further round.

A round price reflects what investors paid for the preferred stock issued in that round. Most shares sold by employees are common stock, which carries fewer rights and typically trades at a discount to the preferred price.
investors: Jane Street and Situational Awareness led the Series B, Spark Capital led the Series A, and Nat Friedman and Daniel Gross led the seed round. Other investors include Triatomic Capital, Harpoon Ventures, Patrick and John Collison, and the supply-chain partners Alchip and Marvell.
spv_sentence: No special purpose vehicles naming MatX appear in SEC Form D filings.
sources: Sources: MatX's Series B announcement; TechCrunch reports dated February 24, 2026 and November 22, 2024; reporting by Reuters (August 2026); and SEC Form D filings.
